photo.caption: A scene depicting javelin throwers, a discus thrower, and a long jumper. This drawing is an early 20th Century copy of a scene found on a Panathenaic amphora from Ancient Greece. British Museum, c. 525 BC.
photo.description: Pentathlon scene from Ancient Greece, featuring two javelin throwers. The first figure holds his javelin at the carry, while the third figure aims with his; the fingering of the amentum is clearly shown on each. Panathenaic amphora, about 525 B.C. British Museum. Image and description source: 'Throwing the Javelin' in Athletics of the Ancient World (1930), Gardiner, E. Norman. Reprinted with corrections, Oxford:Oxford University Press, 1967, p.170, fig. 139.

photo.caption: The throw of this 76kg stone represents the continuity of a ballistic training tradition which dates from Ancient Greece. Unspunnenfest, 1981.

photo.caption: This battle scene found on a Roman sarcophagus demonstrates the excellent physical conditioning of both Roman soldiers and Celtic warriors. Dallas Museum of Art, c. 190 AD.
photo.description: Roman sarcophagus at the Dallas Museum of Art

photo.caption: Schilling (Swiss) mercenaries training, including stone putting, wrestling, skipping, and jumping or diving. Lucerne Chronicle, 1513.
photo.description: The men entertain themselves with games; disciplines depicted are (top to bottom) wrestling, racing, Steinstossen and long jump. The men entertain themselves with games; disciplines depicted are (top to bottom) wrestling, racing, Steinstossen and long jump.

photo.caption: A training scene showing various exercises such as wrestling, fencing, and throwing a stone (stone putting). By Sebald Beham (1500–1550).
photo.description: A scene showing various exercises such as wrestling, fencing, and throwing a stone (stone putting)

photo.caption: This engraving on wood shows gymnastics, monkey bars, and synchronised Indian club swinging being practiced in a large gym run by the YMCA. London, c. 1888.
photo.description: A gym scene showing gymastics, climbing, and Indian club swinging being practiced. Young Men's Christian Association (YMCA) gymnasium, Longacre, London, wood engraving, c. 1888. Opened by the Prince of Wales on June 16, 1888.

photo.caption: Gymnastics, climbing, fencing, and boxing in a commercial gym environment. Roper's gymnasium, Philadelphia, c. 1831.
photo.description: An advertisement for Roper's gymnasium, Philadephia, circa 1831. Note the numerous directions in which the shoulders are exercised; this can help to open up the chest and improve breathing. Note the climbing up the underside of a ladder.
